title: Three-uniform edge-ordered hypergraph quantum states: entanglement and its relation to hypergraph properties
authors: N. A. Susulovska, Kh. P. Gnatenko
abstract: The encoding of 3-uniform edge-ordered weighted hypergraphs into multiqubit quantum states is proposed. We derive an analytical expression for the geometric measure of entanglement of hypergraph quantum states and establish its relation to hypergraph properties. The results establish a direct connection between the local structure of hypergraphs, hyperedge weights, and the entanglement of the corresponding quantum states. For equally weighted hypergraphs, it is shown that the entanglement depends explicitly on the vertex degree. The dependence of entanglement on hypergraph parameters is studied analytically and using quantum computing. Hypergraph states associated with chain, star, regular lattice, and binary-tree hypergraphs are examined, and their entanglement is quantified using quantum computing. These results open up the possibility of studying hypergraph properties with quantum programming.
summary: This paper develops a method to encode 3-uniform hypergraphs into multiqubit quantum states and quantifies the entanglement within these states. It establishes a direct, quantitative link showing that the entanglement of a qubit depends explicitly on the local structure and weights of the hyperedges connected to that vertex. This opens a new avenue for studying graph theory using quantum computation.
main_problem: The paper investigates the relationship between the entanglement properties of multiqubit quantum states and the structural characteristics of the underlying 3-uniform edge-ordered hypergraphs.
main_result: A direct framework is established connecting the entanglement of individual qubits to the local structure (like vertex degree) and the specific weights of the incident hyperedges.
method: The authors derive an analytical expression for the geometric measure of entanglement and apply it to specific hypergraph structures, comparing analytical results with quantum simulation measurements.
model_or_system: The system involves multiqubit quantum states $|\psi_{HG}angle$ encoded from 3-uniform edge-ordered weighted hypergraphs, prepared using parameterized RZZY entangling operators.
key_observables: Geometric measure of entanglement ($E$), expectation values of Pauli observables ($\langle\sigma_x^langle, \langle\sigma_y^langle, \langle\sigma_z^langle$), and the dependence of entanglement on vertex degree.
important_parameters: Hyperedge weights ($	heta_{ijk}$), vertex degree, and the specific connectivity patterns of the hypergraphs (e.g., chain, star, lattice).
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses specifically on 3-uniform hypergraphs, and the state preparation relies on a specific choice of interaction type ($R_{ZZY}$) to ensure a one-to-one mapping.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the structure of various 3-uniform hypergraphs (chain, star, lattice, binary tree) and show the calculated geometric measure of entanglement for specific vertices within these structures.
paper_structure: The paper first proposes the encoding method and derives the entanglement measure. It then analyzes specific, well-known hypergraph topologies (chain, star, lattice, binary tree) by calculating the entanglement for individual qubits based on the incident hyperedge weights. Finally, it confirms consistency between analytical and simulated results.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, mathematically rigorous method to map abstract graph theory properties (hypergraph structure) directly onto measurable quantum information properties (entanglement), which is highly relevant for quantum simulation and resource theory.
